1.title: The Word Made Flesh
1.themes: Deity of Christ, Light vs. Darkness, Witness of John the Baptist, Calling of the First Disciples
1.outline:
I. The Prologue (1:1-18)
II. John the Baptist's Testimony (1:19-34)
III. The First Disciples (1:35-51)
1.summary: John begins with a profound prologue identifying Jesus as the eternal Word (Logos) who became flesh. John the Baptist testifies that Jesus is the Lamb of God. Jesus begins calling his first disciples, including Andrew, Peter, Philip, and Nathanael.

2.title: The First Sign and the Temple Cleansing
2.themes: Miracles (Signs) as Revelation of Glory, New Covenant replacing the Old, Zeal for God's House
2.outline:
I. The Wedding at Cana (2:1-12)
II. Cleansing the Temple (2:13-25)
2.summary: Jesus performs his first public miracle, turning water into wine at a wedding in Cana, symbolizing the joy and abundance of the new covenant. He then goes to Jerusalem and drives the merchants out of the temple, prophesying about his resurrection.

3.title: The New Birth
3.themes: Regeneration (Born Again), God's Love for the World, Spiritual vs. Fleshly Birth, John the Baptist's Humility
3.outline:
I. Jesus and Nicodemus (3:1-21)
II. John the Baptist's Final Testimony (3:22-36)
3.summary: Nicodemus, a Pharisee, visits Jesus at night. Jesus teaches him that one must be 'born again' (or 'born from above') to see the kingdom of God. This chapter contains the famous verse John 3:16. John the Baptist rejoices at Jesus' growing ministry, saying 'He must increase, but I must decrease.'

4.title: The Woman at the Well
4.themes: Living Water, True Worship, Breaking Social/Racial Barriers, The Harvest
4.outline:
I. Jesus and the Samaritan Woman (4:1-26)
II. The Disciples and the Harvest (4:27-38)
III. The Samaritans Believe (4:39-42)
IV. Healing the Official's Son (4:43-54)
4.summary: Jesus travels through Samaria and speaks with a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well, offering her 'living water.' She believes he is the Messiah and brings her village to him. Back in Galilee, Jesus performs his second sign by healing an official's son from a distance.

5.title: Healing at the Pool of Bethesda
5.themes: Sabbath Controversy, Equality with the Father, Life and Judgment, Witnesses to Christ
5.outline:
I. The Healing at the Pool (5:1-15)
II. Jesus Claims Equality with God (5:16-30)
III. Testimonies about Jesus (5:31-47)
5.summary: Jesus heals a man who had been invalid for 38 years on the Sabbath. This leads to persecution by Jewish leaders. Jesus responds by claiming a unique relationship with God the Father, asserting his authority to give life and judge, and citing multiple witnesses to his identity.

6.title: The Bread of Life
6.themes: Jesus as the Bread of Life, Spiritual vs. Physical Food, Sovereignty in Salvation, Defection of Disciples
6.outline:
I. Feeding the Five Thousand (6:1-15)
II. Jesus Walks on Water (6:16-21)
III. The Bread of Life Discourse (6:22-59)
IV. Reactions to the Teaching (6:60-71)
6.summary: After multiplying loaves and fishes and walking on water, Jesus delivers a difficult discourse, claiming he is the 'bread of life' and that one must eat his flesh and drink his blood. Many followers find this teaching too hard and leave him, but Peter confesses Jesus has the 'words of eternal life.'

7.title: The Feast of Booths
7.themes: Division over Jesus, Living Water, Divine Timing (Jesus' 'Hour'), Unbelief of Brothers
7.outline:
I. Jesus goes Secretly to the Feast (7:1-13)
II. Jesus Teaches in the Temple (7:14-36)
III. Promise of the Holy Spirit (7:37-39)
IV. Division Among the People (7:40-53)
7.summary: Despite threats to his life, Jesus attends the Feast of Booths in Jerusalem. He teaches openly, causing widespread debate about whether he is the Prophet or the Christ. On the last day of the feast, he cries out offering the Holy Spirit as rivers of living water to those who believe.

8.title: The Light of the World
8.themes: Jesus as the Light, Spiritual Fatherhood (God vs. Satan), Truth and Freedom, The 'I Am' Statement
8.outline:
I. The Woman Caught in Adultery (8:1-11)
II. Jesus the Light of the World (8:12-30)
III. True Disciples and True Children of Abraham (8:31-47)
IV. Jesus' Pre-existence (8:48-59)
8.summary: After dealing mercifully with a woman caught in adultery, Jesus declares 'I am the light of the world.' A fierce debate with Jewish leaders ensues regarding spiritual lineage. Jesus tells them the truth will set them free and dramatically claims eternal existence before Abraham ('I am').

9.title: Healing of the Man Born Blind
9.themes: Spiritual Blindness vs. Sight, The Problem of Suffering, Cost of Discipleship
9.outline:
I. The Healing (9:1-12)
II. Investigation by the Pharisees (9:13-34)
III. Spiritual Blindness (9:35-41)
9.summary: Jesus heals a man born blind, stating that his blindness was for God's works to be displayed. The Pharisees launch a hostile investigation and ultimately excommunicate the healed man. Jesus reveals himself as the Son of Man to the outcast, while declaring the Pharisees to be spiritually blind.

10.title: The Good Shepherd
10.themes: Jesus as the Shepherd and the Door, Intimacy with the Flock, Security of the Believer, Deity of Christ
10.outline:
I. The Good Shepherd Discourse (10:1-21)
II. Conflict at the Feast of Dedication (10:22-42)
10.summary: Jesus describes himself as the Good Shepherd who lays down his life for his sheep, contrasting himself with thieves and hired hands. Later, at the Feast of Dedication, he states plainly 'I and the Father are one,' prompting the religious leaders to attempt to stone him for blasphemy.

11.title: The Resurrection of Lazarus
11.themes: Resurrection and Life, Jesus' Power over Death, Divine Timing, The Final Catalyst for the Plot against Jesus
11.outline:
I. The Death of Lazarus (11:1-16)
II. Jesus the Resurrection and the Life (11:17-37)
III. Raising Lazarus (11:38-44)
IV. The Plot to Kill Jesus (11:45-57)
11.summary: Lazarus, a dear friend of Jesus, falls ill and dies. Jesus delays his arrival, later proclaiming to Martha, 'I am the resurrection and the life.' He raises Lazarus from the tomb after four days. This stunning miracle becomes the tipping point for the Sanhedrin, who officially plot to kill him.

12.title: The Triumphal Entry and the Coming Hour
12.themes: Devotion to Christ, Prophetic Fulfillment, The Grain of Wheat, The Judgment of the World
12.outline:
I. Mary Anoints Jesus (12:1-11)
II. The Triumphal Entry (12:12-19)
III. Jesus Predicts His Death (12:20-36)
IV. The Unbelief of the People (12:37-50)
12.summary: Mary anoints Jesus with expensive ointment at Bethany. Jesus enters Jerusalem to adoring crowds. When some Greeks seek him, Jesus declares his 'hour' has come, using the metaphor of a dying seed producing much fruit. Despite his signs, many refuse to believe, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecies.

13.title: Washing the Disciples' Feet
13.themes: Servant Leadership, Love for One Another, Betrayal, The Upper Room Discourse begins
13.outline:
I. Jesus Washes His Disciples' Feet (13:1-20)
II. Jesus Predicts His Betrayal (13:21-30)
III. The New Commandment (13:31-35)
IV. Jesus Predicts Peter's Denial (13:36-38)
13.summary: During the Last Supper, Jesus models ultimate humility by washing his disciples' feet. He predicts that Judas will betray him and that Peter will deny him. He gives his followers a new commandment: to love one another just as he has loved them.

14.title: The Way, the Truth, and the Life
14.themes: Comfort in Christ, Jesus as the Only Way, The Promise of the Holy Spirit (Paraclete), Peace
14.outline:
I. Jesus the Way to the Father (14:1-14)
II. The Promise of the Holy Spirit (14:15-31)
14.summary: Jesus comforts his troubled disciples, promising to prepare a place for them and declaring himself 'the way, and the truth, and the life.' He promises to send the Holy Spirit, the Helper, who will dwell within them, and he leaves them with his supernatural peace.

15.title: The True Vine
15.themes: Abiding in Christ, Fruitfulness, The World's Hatred, Friendship with Jesus
15.outline:
I. The Vine and the Branches (15:1-17)
II. The Hatred of the World (15:18-27)
15.summary: Using the metaphor of the vine and the branches, Jesus emphasizes the absolute necessity of abiding in him to produce spiritual fruit. He calls his disciples 'friends.' He also warns them that just as the world hated him, it will hate them, but the Spirit will bear witness.

16.title: The Work of the Holy Spirit
16.themes: The Ministry of the Spirit, Overcoming the World, Grief Turning to Joy, Prayer in Jesus' Name
16.outline:
I. The Work of the Holy Spirit (16:1-15)
II. Sorrow will Turn into Joy (16:16-24)
III. Jesus has Overcome the World (16:25-33)
16.summary: Jesus explains that it is to their advantage that he leaves, so the Helper will come. The Spirit will convict the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment. Jesus assures them that their coming sorrow will turn to profound joy, concluding with the victory cry: 'I have overcome the world.'

17.title: The High Priestly Prayer
17.themes: Glory, Unity, Sanctification in Truth, Jesus' Intercession for Believers
17.outline:
I. Jesus Prays for Himself (17:1-5)
II. Jesus Prays for His Disciples (17:6-19)
III. Jesus Prays for All Future Believers (17:20-26)
17.summary: In his longest recorded prayer, Jesus asks the Father to glorify him. He prays for the protection and sanctification of his disciples. He then extends his prayer to all who will ever believe in him through their message, praying passionately for their unity so the world may believe.

18.title: Betrayal, Arrest, and Trial
18.themes: Jesus' Sovereign Control, Two Kingdoms, Truth, Fulfilling the Father's Cup
18.outline:
I. Betrayal and Arrest (18:1-11)
II. Jesus Before Annas and Peter's Denials (18:12-27)
III. Jesus Before Pilate (18:28-40)
18.summary: Judas leads soldiers to the garden, where Jesus willingly surrenders, asserting his 'I am' identity. Peter denies knowing Jesus. Jesus is taken before Annas and Caiaphas, and then to Pilate, where he declares that his kingdom is not of this world and that he came to bear witness to the truth.

19.title: Crucifixion and Burial
19.themes: Substitutionary Atonement, Fulfillment of Scripture, The Finished Work of Christ
19.outline:
I. Jesus is Scourged and Condemned (19:1-16)
II. The Crucifixion (19:17-27)
III. The Death of Jesus (19:28-37)
IV. The Burial (19:38-42)
19.summary: Pilate gives in to the crowd and sentences Jesus to death. Jesus is crucified at Golgotha. After ensuring his mother is cared for by John, he drinks the sour wine and cries out, 'It is finished.' Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus respectfully bury his body in a new tomb.

20.title: The Resurrection
20.themes: Triumph over Death, Believing without Seeing, Commissioning the Disciples, The Purpose of the Gospel
20.outline:
I. The Empty Tomb (20:1-10)
II. Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene (20:11-18)
III. Jesus Appears to the Disciples (20:19-23)
IV. Jesus and Thomas (20:24-29)
V. The Purpose of the Book (20:30-31)
20.summary: Mary Magdalene finds the tomb empty. Jesus appears first to her, then to the disciples behind locked doors, breathing the Holy Spirit on them. A week later, he appears to 'Doubting Thomas,' who confesses him as 'My Lord and my God!' John explicitly states the Gospel was written so readers may believe and have life.

21.title: Epilogue: Restoration and Commission
21.themes: Restoration of the Fallen, Feeding the Flock, Following Christ without Comparison
21.outline:
I. The Miraculous Catch of Fish (21:1-14)
II. Jesus Restores Peter (21:15-19)
III. The Beloved Disciple and Conclusion (21:20-25)
21.summary: In a post-resurrection appearance by the Sea of Galilee, Jesus provides a miraculous catch of fish. He gently restores Peter, who had denied him three times, by asking him three times if he loves him, instructing him to 'feed my sheep.' The Gospel ends affirming the truthfulness of the disciple's testimony.
